summary: The finite-verb suppression on branch A2 (ab95a4f) closes R1 and R2 cleanly: every headline that previously false-dropped ('Video of the X reveal leaked online' and its two siblings, 'First hands-on video of the 2027 Corvette Z06...') now resolves to a plain PUBLISH, not even a hold. The 'watch' NP-branch fix (code-reviewer's 'Watch this space...' finding) is independently verified fixed. The policy split (d4eac81) means the one remaining ambiguous case I found in round 2 ('Unboxing the mystery behind...') no longer matters at the severity I flagged it at -- it now resolves to HOLD, costing a button press instead of losing the story. Attacking the split specifically confirms the coordinator's framing is exactly right: video_lead (colon-form 'Vídeo:'/'Watch:') is now the ONLY branch that can still cause irreversible loss, and it is structurally still reachable by a genuine-news headline -- but only through a narrow, deliberate editorial convention ('WATCH:'/'VIDEO:' as a headline prefix) that in real-world online journalism is used almost exclusively to flag actual video content, and which the operator explicitly, by name, required to stay unconditional ('Watch: first look at the 2027 HW Nationals mainline' must still drop). I could not construct a headline in this shape that reads as clearly non-video content without resorting to a stretch (an editorial 'Watch:' used as a pure attention-getter for a text listicle) that has no precedent in the four cited source styles. The hold path is verified genuinely real end-to-end via two independent routes: the existing job()-level integration tests (all pass) and my own from-scratch repo-layer probe bypassing job() entirely. Suite is 1574 passed / 435 subtests, identical across two runs. Recommending ship, with the video_lead colon-convention noted as a residual, low-probability, and explicitly-accepted trade-off rather than a blocker.

action_table.note: ACTION is the real end-state the content gate alone would produce (publish / hold / drop), computed by mirroring job()'s exact decision order: _hold_for_review_reason -> _is_rejected_genre -> _GENRE_BRANCH_ACTION lookup. 'publish' means the content gate does not stop the article (later gates such as dedup are out of scope here, as in rounds 1-2).

video_lead_attack.question: Is there any headline that still lands in video_lead (the only remaining irreversible branch) while being genuine news?
video_lead_attack.answer: Yes, structurally -- but only through the deliberate, explicit 'Vídeo:'/'Watch:' colon-prefix convention the operator required to stay unconditional, not through an accidental grammatical seam like R1/R2. All 6 attack headlines still drop via video_lead. I could not find a realistic headline in the 4 cited source styles (autoevolution/lamley/t-hunted/orangetrack) that uses a bare 'Watch:'/'Vídeo:' colon-lead for genuinely non-video content -- in real online-journalism convention that specific prefix is reserved almost universally for actual video content, which is presumably why the operator picked it as the one unambiguous, no-judgement-required signal.

cases.assessment: Control case -- exact shape of the operator's own required case. Correctly still drops; A1 has no verb-suppression by design, and that is intentional (only A2 needed it, because A2's NP-heads are ALSO how a news clause names its subject).

cases.headline: Vídeo: fotos e detalhes completos do novo Camaro revelado
cases.assessment: Minor asymmetry worth noting: the comma-led sibling of this exact headline ('Vídeo, fotos e detalhes...', tested in round 2) correctly survives, because the comma separator regex only recognises colon/hyphen/en-dash/em-dash. The colon variant of an otherwise-identical multi-asset list headline drops. Narrow, low-frequency stylistic difference (comma vs colon after the lead word) -- flagging for awareness, not blocking.

cases.headline: Watch: five 2026 Treasure Hunts you might have missed on pegs
cases.assessment: The closest thing to a genuine miss I could construct: 'Watch:' used as a pure editorial imperative ('pay attention to:') for a text/photo roundup with no actual video asset. I rate this LOW real-world probability for this specific niche -- the 'WATCH:' headline prefix is an extremely strong, near-universal online-journalism convention specifically for video content, and I found no precedent for it being used as a bare attention-getter in the cited source styles. Still, it is the one case where the branch's unconditional nature (no verb-suppression) could theoretically misfire on non-video content, unlike A2 which now has that suppression.

test_suite_stability.verified: Ran the full suite twice independently: run 1 = 1574 passed, 435 subtests passed (53.21s); run 2 = 1574 passed, 435 subtests passed (49.67s). Identical pass count both times, no flakes, no skips.

residual_risk_one_sentence: The only remaining irreversible-loss surface is the colon-form video_lead branch ('Vídeo:'/'Watch:' + separator, unconditional by design), which is structurally reachable by genuine non-video content in principle but in practice matches a narrow, deliberate editorial convention that real automotive-journalism headlines reserve almost exclusively for actual video content, and which the operator explicitly required to stay unconditional with their own named test case.

ship_recommendation.reasoning: Both round-1 (F1/F2) and round-2 (R1/R2) false-drop findings are now fully closed -- not merely demoted to hold, but resolved to plain publish, which is the strongest possible fix. The one round-2 finding that remains structurally reachable ('Unboxing the mystery behind...', R4) now costs a button press instead of the article, because of the policy split -- exactly the mitigation the coordinator's proposed design was meant to provide, and it works as advertised end-to-end (verified two independent ways). Attacking the one remaining unconditional-drop branch (video_lead) surfaced only a narrow, low-probability, and explicitly-operator-accepted trade-off, not a fresh instance of the F1/R1 bug class. Suite is green and stable. I see no remaining blocking issue.
